content: Skin cancer is a malignant growth that occurs on the skin and can arise from various causes. It typically develops in the epidermis, which is the outermost layer of the skin. Because of its location, tumors associated with skin cancer are often visible, allowing for early detection in most cases. There are three primary types of skin cancer, each named after the specific type of skin cell from which it originates. Skin cancer is currently the fastest-growing type of cancer in the United States and is the most frequently diagnosed malignancy, surpassing lung, breast, colorectal, and prostate cancers. In 2007 alone, over one million Americans were expected to be diagnosed with skin cancer. The most prevalent forms of skin cancer are basal cell carcinoma (BCC) and squamous cell carcinoma (SCC). While these types of skin cancer can cause local tissue damage and disfigurement, they are generally unlikely to metastasize, or spread to other parts of the body. Malignant melanoma, on the other hand, is the most dangerous form of skin cancer. If not treated promptly, malignant melanoma can be fatal, although it accounts for only a small percentage of all skin cancer cases. Other, less common types of skin cancer include dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans, Merkel cell carcinoma, and Kaposi's sarcoma.
